revisit_notes: Representative 12-thruster layout (8 tangential + 2 prograde + 2 retro), not the flight layout (which needs the layout drawing, absent per SATURN-SHIP-SPEC.md note 1). The conclusion needs the flight layout to have tangential authority about both in-plane axes -- a generic requirement any 3-axis-couple RCS meets; a real layout only adds authority.

The H1 in-plane result is exact for r_off || boom; boom sway alpha tilts the dump axis out of plane by ~sin(alpha) (0.34 at 20 deg). The out-of-plane component is a yaw-like torque coverable by tangential x-y couples (sideways plume); only a pathological >45 deg sway would demand retro thrust. Sway is bounded by the cinch/grapple stiffness -- a capture-mechanics parameter.

Parametrized plume model (P~F/r^2, cos^n forward, beta backflow) inherited from R-berth-plume-impingement -- same model-robustness caveat: the ~100x H2 margin and the tangential-vs-retro geometry distinction survive any plausible plume shape; exact Pa would need DSMC.

Simultaneous-firing bound: a couple fires <=4 tangential thrusters; even the naive sum (4 x per-thruster max ~0.022) = 0.09 N.m << 2.5, so the exact control-allocation cannot break the bound -- the result is allocation-independent for any tangential-only couple.

verdict.summary: The momentum-management thread CLOSES. Because the capture arm is along the boom, the injected momentum is structurally in the boom-perpendicular plane (H1), so every required dump axis is in-plane. In-plane torque couples are realizable from tangential thrusters whose plumes point sideways (~90 deg to the forward bag), giving a max bag-plume torque of ~0.04 N.m over all azimuths -- 66x under the 2.5 N.m re-perturbation threshold (H2). The retro (-z) thrusters are the only plume-danger (~1.5 N.m, plume core) and are avoidable: the tangential set spans +/- torque about both in-plane axes (H3). So leg A (thruster dump) is UNCONDITIONALLY viable for the physically-required dump axes, secured by a cheap plume-aware control-allocation rule (build the couple from tangential thrusters, deprioritize retro) plus a grapple boom >= 3 m -- NO new hardware. Legs B (CMG, ~300-600 kg) and C (precision capture) are retired to optional risk reduction. The only residual is a flight-layout confirmation that tangential authority exists about both in-plane axes (generic for any 3-axis-couple RCS).
